transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about?

I guess what brings me in is... I don’t really feel happiness or closeness anymore. Even when my wife tries to get me to enjoy things we used to do on Sundays, or when something goes well at work, I just don’t feel much. It’s like I know I should feel good, but I don’t.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities that you used to enjoy, like the things you mentioned doing on Sundays with your wife?

Yes. That’s probably the main thing I’ve noticed. The Sunday stuff with my wife used to feel good, like something I looked forward to, but now I just kind of go through it. And even if something goes well at work, I know it’s supposed to feel satisfying, but I don’t really feel happy or connected to it.
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, even when nothing particularly bad is happening?
I’m not sure I’d say sad most of the day, nearly every day. It’s more like I feel flat or kind of empty. I don’t always notice it as sadness exactly.
Have you noticed that you feel fatigued or that you’ve lost your energy, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically or mentally taxing?
I don’t think I’ve really noticed that specifically. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, but I can’t say I’ve felt unusually drained when I haven’t done much.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or thinking clearly, even when you're not particularly stressed or tired?
Not really, no. I mean, I have moments where I lose my train of thought like anyone, but I haven’t noticed a clear problem with concentrating when I’m not stressed or tired.
Have you found yourself feeling worthless or guilty, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

Yeah… not exactly worthless, but guilty, I guess. I keep thinking I can’t trust my own judgment anymore. Like if I miss one small detail on a schedule or a machine setting, somebody could get hurt because of me. It’s hard to shake that.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or alternatively, feeling restless or fidgety, as if you can’t sit still?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself moving slower than usual, and I wouldn’t say I’m especially fidgety or unable to sit still.
How long have you been feeling this way—like you don’t experience happiness or closeness anymore?
Since the retrofit accident… so about a year and seven months now. It’s been pretty constant since then.

Would you say that you've completely lost interest in the activities you used to enjoy on Sundays with your wife, or do you still find some value or benefit in doing them even if you don’t feel happiness?

I still do them sometimes because I know they matter to my wife, and I guess there’s some value in keeping the routine. But I don’t really feel happy from it anymore. Even when it should be nice, or when something goes well at work, I don’t feel that real happiness or closeness like I used to.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in nearly all activities, not just the ones you used to do on Sundays?

Yeah… it’s broader than just Sundays. I still do things when I have to, or because they matter to my wife, but I don’t really get pleasure from them. Even if something goes well at work, I don’t feel happy the way I used to. It’s like that feeling just doesn’t really come.
Would you say that your lack of pleasure or interest in activities has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks or more?

Yes. It’s there most of the day, pretty much every day. I can go through the motions, but I don’t feel real happiness or closeness anymore—even when my wife tries to get me into our old Sunday routines, or when something goes well at work.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over the past several months—like eating much less or much more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?
I haven’t really noticed a big change there. My appetite might go up and down a little, but I’m not aware of any significant weight loss or gain.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep—like trouble falling asleep, waking up frequently during the night, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, sleep has been bad. Most nights I’m lying there replaying the plant in my head, and if I do fall asleep, I’ll jolt awake from dreams about the line. A lot of nights I’m up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and it feels like I never really rested.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you didn’t feel happiness or closeness, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

This is the first time it’s felt like this. I mean, I’ve had rough periods before, but not where I just don’t feel real happiness or closeness. Even the things that used to matter—like Sundays with my wife, or doing well at work—just don’t really reach me now.
Have you ever felt so low or hopeless that you’ve thought about hurting yourself or ending your life?
I… I’m not really sure how to answer that. I’ve felt really low, yeah, but I don’t know that I’ve had clear thoughts like that. I haven’t made any plans or anything like that.
Have you had days when you felt this lack of happiness and closeness so intensely that it affected your ability to function normally at work or at home?

Yes. It’s gotten in the way pretty badly. At work I’ve had to hand off floor responsibilities I used to handle myself. And during an interview with a regional director, I just… lost it. I couldn’t keep myself together and I walked out.

At home, it’s affecting things too. My wife can tell I’m there, but not really there. I’m not really participating in our life the way I used to, and it’s putting a strain on us.
Between the time you started feeling this way after the retrofit accident and now, have you had a period of at least two months where you felt back to your usual self, without these symptoms?
No. Since the retrofit accident, it’s pretty much been ongoing. That was about a year and seven months ago, and I haven’t had a stretch of two months where I felt like myself again.

Since the time you started feeling this way after the retrofit accident, have you ever had a period of at least two months where you felt completely back to your usual self, without any of these symptoms?
No, not really. Since the retrofit accident, it’s just been going on. That was about a year and seven months ago, and I haven’t had a couple months where I felt completely back to normal.

Would you say that during the past year and seven months, there were times when your mood was low enough that you could describe it as a major depressive episode, lasting at least two weeks at a time?

I’m not sure I’d know how to separate it that way. My mood has definitely been low at times, but whether it was a full episode for two weeks or more… I don’t know. I haven’t really tracked it like that.
